sections.description: This section introduces the patient, her medical history, the immediate adverse reaction to semaglutide, and her subsequent progressive clinical decline. It also covers the necessary background on GLP-1 receptor agonists and the clinical and pathological characteristics of immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM) to provide context for the case.
subtopics: Patient's past medical history (obesity, NAFLD, hypothyroidism) and baseline functional status
Immediate reaction to the initial dose of semaglutide (GI symptoms, acute renal failure, mild CK elevation)
Progressive clinical deterioration over 4 months (dysphagia, dysphonia, proximal muscle weakness)
Overview of GLP-1 receptor agonists: indications, common side effects, and known muscle-related effects
Pathophysiology and clinical features of IMNM (proximal weakness, CK elevation, paucity of lymphocytic infiltrates, association with HMGCR/SRP antibodies)

sections.description: This section details the comprehensive workup performed to diagnose the cause of the patient's progressive muscle weakness. It covers the laboratory tests, imaging studies, and tissue biopsies that led to the histological confirmation of IMNM and helped rule out other potential etiologies.
subtopics: Laboratory findings: significant CK elevation, liver enzymes, autoantibody panels (ANA, myositis panel including anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR), and inflammatory markers
Musculoskeletal imaging: MRI of bilateral femurs showing muscular edema
Cardiac evaluation: echocardiogram and cardiac MRI findings suggesting potential myocardial involvement
Histopathological confirmation: muscle biopsy findings (necrotic/regenerating fibers, CD68 macrophage staining, membrane attack complex, rare CD3 cells)
Liver biopsy findings to explain transaminitis and differentiate hepatic vs. muscle sources of elevated transaminases

sections.description: This section explores the clinical reasoning used to differentiate IMNM from other myopathic and inflammatory processes. It critically evaluates the temporal relationship between semaglutide exposure and symptom onset to assess drug causality.
subtopics: Differentiating IMNM from drug-induced rhabdomyolysis (timeline, CK trends, and histology)
Ruling out other etiologies: toxic myopathy, statin-induced myopathy (despite no statin use), and idiopathic autoimmune myopathy
Evaluating the significance of the isolated low-titer SS-B antibody
Assessing cardiac findings: myocarditis vs. stress-induced cardiomyopathy
Applying WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) causality criteria to semaglutide and IMNM

sections.description: This section outlines the acute and longitudinal management of the patient's IMNM. It explains the rationale behind the chosen immunosuppressive regimen and details the subsequent clinical outcomes, including treatment complications and the patient's functional recovery.
subtopics: Acute treatment: pulse IV methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone
Adjunctive therapy: administration of IVIG and the rationale for its use in severe IMNM
Monitoring response: rapid decline in CK levels and improvement in muscle strength
Management of complications: hospitalization for septic shock (pseudomonal UTI) and its resolution
Outpatient follow-up, rapid tapering of immunosuppression, and sustained remission off medication

sections.description: This final section synthesizes the key takeaways from the case. It focuses on the implications for clinical practice regarding the expanding use of GLP-1 receptor agonists and the importance of recognizing rare immune-mediated adverse drug reactions.
subtopics: The contrast in clinical courses between toxic rhabdomyolysis and immune-mediated necrotising myopathy
The role of drug cessation and short-course immunosuppression in drug-induced IMNM vs. idiopathic IMNM
Importance of pharmacovigilance with newly popular medications (GLP-1 agonists)
Considerations for future research: identifying predisposing factors for drug-induced IMNM
Ethical considerations regarding drug rechallenge in severe adverse reactions
